newsitem.title: FRANCE: First French soldiers sail for Albania.
newsitem.headline: First French soldiers sail for Albania.

text.p: The first soldiers of the French contingent of a multinational security force for Albania started leaving on Tuesday for the Balkan state's port of Durres, military sources said.
They said the scouts sailed aboard the navy transport ship Champlain from the French Mediterranean port of Toulon.
The bulk of the 1,000-strong French contingent was gathering at Miramas, near Marseille, and would leave from Toulon on Friday to reach Durres early next week.
The French marines, backed by combat engineers, will be equipped with armoured vehicles and helicopters.

The French contingent will be part of a force approved by the United Nations to protect relief convoys in Albania, which has been wracked by violence in a rebellion prompted by the collapse of popular but fraudulent pyramid savings schemes.
The 6,000-strong Italian-led force, being sent to protect humanitarian aid, is expected to start its mission in the lawless Balkan state around April 14.
Italy is expected to provide 2,000 to 2,500 troops, France 1,000, Greece 700, Turkey 500, Spain 500 and Romania 400.
